not_judged.TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) always sets ADDR_WIDTH, to 4 and to 8 (lines 75, 1121 and 1122), so the default is never used and widths 5 to 7 are never built; a block whose default is 5, or that aliases offsets from 0x10 up only at width 6, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-PORTS-ONLY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) connects the ports by name (lines 75 to 83), and Icarus Verilog builds an instance that leaves a port of the block unconnected, so a block with an extra port passes it. The widths of the named ports are checked (lines 461 to 480, TMR-PORTS).
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-READ: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks the value of COUNT while a count runs: it compares COUNT with a value only at reset, after a one-shot count ends, after a COUNT write and after a stop (lines 314, 298, 331, 403 to 404, 409, 457, 529, 575, 577, 579 and 587). The two reads of a running COUNT (lines 428 and 430) check only that RDATA and RRESP hold still while RVALID waits and that the response is OKAY. The coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1112) likewise compares COUNT only with the count stopped: in its write sweep, where no count runs (line 798), after a one-shot count ends, and after a stop (lines 913, 958 and 1021). COUNT's value during a count is judged only through the edge the count ends on (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH) and the value a stop leaves (TMR-STOP-EDGE).
not_judged.TMR-CTRL-WINS: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lands a CTRL write on the edge a count ends: its only writes timed to a count end are the STATUS clears at lines 395 to 398 and 441 to 444, and the stops of its periodic runs are checked to land before the next count end (lines 602 and 617). In the coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1112), the STATUS clears of each traced count land on count ends by design (lines 970 to 1028, TMR-END-BEATS-CLEAR), the stops of its periodic counts are checked to land before the next count end (lines 957 and 1020), a periodic count of LOAD 0 to 2, where every edge or every other one ends a count, is ended by a reset with no transfer in progress instead of a stop (line 1007), and its CTRL write matrix runs with LOAD 0x0010_0000, which never ends inside it. No mutant breaks this rule.
not_judged.TMR-READ-VALUE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks a value read on an edge on which that register changes: COUNT only while it holds still (see TMR-COUNT-READ; the reads of a running COUNT at lines 428 and 430 check no value), CTRL and STATUS only on edges on which no count ends, LOAD never during a write. So a read that returns the value after the accepting edge is not caught. The coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1112) keeps to the same: its overlapped reads (lines 1030 to 1064) read CTRL or an unmapped address while LOAD or an unmapped address is written.
not_judged.TMR-RESET-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) drives aresetn low only at power up, where BVALID, RVALID and the held halves start unknown rather than high, and in the middle of a count with no transfer in progress (lines 274 to 282, 308 to 310 and 450 to 454), and in the coverage matrix between transfers, at its start and to end a periodic count of LOAD 0 to 2 (lines 1093 and 1007), changing it only between rising edges. So it never sees a pending response or a held half write dropped by reset, and does not tell a synchronous reset from an asynchronous one. The manager rule is an assumption on the testbench, which keeps it.
not_judged.TMR-CLEAN: Lint and synthesis are the RTL stage's own before-review checks, not held-out checks.
not_judged.TMR-TB-ALL: The must-fail check holds the flow's testbench to passing on the reference RTL and failing the four committed timer mutants (cited under mutants), and to nothing more: a testbench that leaves any other requirement of sections 2 to 6 unchecked, or times only some counts to the edge, still passes it.
